title: RFC004 §33.7 Review Candidate wrapper (AST Builder design §2.5, spec-ast-builder-t5-promotion T7b/P4)
$comment: Produced by review_candidate.build_review_candidate: the same _build_raw tree as build_strict (same derivations, same binder, same required-property gate), never canonicalized and never given an ast_hash (R10) -- authoritative is always false and this wrapper never enters compile_docx. Every UNRESOLVED_REQUIRED_PROPERTY issue whose default_policy.lookup(...) says may_impute becomes one imputations row and is removed from unresolved; every other issue (RESOURCE_SLOT_UNRESOLVED, NOTE_REF_UNBOUND, STORY_UNRESOLVED, ASSEMBLER_PROPERTY_CONFLICT, and any UNRESOLVED_REQUIRED_PROPERTY default_policy has no record for or refuses to impute) stays in unresolved. builder_report_hash equals the SAME raw build's report_hash (plan U1) -- the strict and review passes agree on it because both walk _build_raw before either the strict gate or this module's imputation post-pass runs. candidate keeps the builder's own b<n> ids and is validated only as an RFC001-shaped tree here, not against canonical_ast.schema.json -- it may be incomplete.

authoritative.$comment: R10: never true -- a review candidate is never the authoritative AST and never carries an ast_hash.

candidate_tree.$comment: The RFC001 root shape _build_raw always writes (ast_builder.py's _build_raw literal), not canonical_ast.schema.json -- a candidate may still have UNRESOLVED_REQUIRED_PROPERTY gaps and is never merged/reordered. footnotes/endnotes are optional (only present when the document carries notes).

unresolved_row.$comment: node_id is nullable: ASSEMBLER_PROPERTY_CONFLICT and STORY_UNRESOLVED are not scoped to one already-built node (BuilderIssue.node_id, ast_builder.py).
